Subject: Where does our data run (regions + subprocessors)?

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — CloudHealth Medical liked the latency numbers. Before we move to an internal security review, the procurement and engineering teams need a concise view of where customer requests (inference and embeddings) are executed, which subprocessors are touched, and whether any cross-border transfers occur for US customers.

Specific asks: 
- A per-region list of execution locations (US/EU/APAC) for hosted vs dedicated deployments.
- Which subprocessors might see request data (e.g., cloud providers, monitoring, logging, analytics).
- Any transient hops outside the requesting region (for routing/fallbacks) and whether keys or customer data are exported.
- Retention and deletion signal: how quickly can data be deleted on request from a tenant and what subprocessors get the deletion command.

If you have a short evidence pack (diagram + inventory spreadsheet), that would speed up our internal review.

Appreciate it — Oliver

--

Mina / Marissa — draft below + attachments attached. Notes from infra: 

Summary (draft):
- Hosted API: For US-region requests we execute in our US cloud region (primary: us-west-2). We maintain EU and APAC hosted regions; requests routed by region.
- Dedicated: Customers with Dedicated capacity run in their pinned region/hardware (no cross-region routing unless customer enables multi-region failover).
- Subprocessors: primary cloud provider (AWS) for compute, CloudLog (logging/observability), Sentry (errors) and Segment (optional analytics). We list versions/contacts in the inventory spreadsheet.
- Transient hops: we do not persist customer request payloads outside the execution region for hosted US requests except for cache-miss routing and model fallback which may briefly route to the nearest available compatible variant (we fall back to another US zone before crossing to EU). Cross-border to EU/APAC only happens when customer selects those regions or when region capacity forces fallback and an explicit policy allows it (we document fallback chains).
- Keys & secrets: private keys never leave our KMS; exports to subprocessors are limited to hashed identifiers for telemetry where applicable.
- Deletion: tenant-initiated deletion triggers orchestration to delete data from primary runtime storage, prefix/KV caches, and issues delete notifications to subprocessors with SLA targets: runtime TTL < 10 minutes for ephemeral caches, analytics logs purge request within 48 hours, and complete propagation in 7 days depending on subprocessor retention policies (see spreadsheet).

I'll attach: redwood_region_map_v2.pdf (map + fallback policy), subprocessors_inventory_2026.xlsx (contacts + retention/SLAs), and k2-dataflow-diagram.png (sequence diagram).

If you want, I can tighten the deletion SLO language (we should avoid promising guarantees that subprocessors cannot meet).

— Ben

Hi Oliver — thanks again and great to hear the demo went well. Attaching a concise evidence pack and an executive summary below. See attachments: redwood_region_map_v2.pdf, subprocessors_inventory_2026.xlsx, k2-dataflow-diagram.png.

Executive summary (for procurement/security):
- Where we run: Hosted API requests from US customers are executed in our US-hosted region (primary us-west-2). We operate EU and APAC hosted regions; routing is region-first. Dedicated capacity runs in the customer’s pinned region/hardware and does not cross-region unless the customer enables multi-region failover.

- Which subprocessors see request data: Primary compute (AWS EC2/EKS), logging/observability (CloudLog), error monitoring (Sentry), analytics (Segment — optional and opted-in). A full inventory with contractual contact and retention commitments is in the spreadsheet.

- Cross-border behavior: We do not route US-hosted requests to EU/APAC unless (a) the customer selects a non-US region, or (b) an automated fallback policy requires routing because US capacity is exhausted and the customer has allowed fallback. Our default fallback order favors other US availability zones/regions before considering cross-border options; cross-border fallbacks are logged and surfaced in the console.

- Keys and secrets: Customer keys remain in our KMS. No plaintext customer request data is exported to subprocessors; telemetry and metrics are pseudonymized/hashed before we forward to analytics providers.

- Deletion & retention: Tenant deletion requests trigger runtime deletion for ephemeral stores immediately. We target: 10 minutes for cache eviction commands, 48 hours to propagate deletion requests to analytics/logging subprocessors, and full propagation within 7 days except where subprocessors have legal/regulatory holds. The spreadsheet flags subprocessors with longer retention windows. For Private deployments we will not forward data to third-party subprocessors without explicit customer opt-in.

Next steps: If this addresses the team's asks I can open a HubSpot record and provide a redacted SOC2 evidence excerpt and a one-page diagram formatted for your security team. If procurement needs contractual language, loop in your legal contact and we’ll coordinate on data processing addendum (DPA) items.
